transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Elysian - Head ML), Tara O'Neill (CTO), Diego Ramos (Lead Data Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Elysian is evaluating Redwood for multi-lingual customer support and document understanding. Key constraints: 32k+ context for long documents, tool-calling for retrieval/plugins, and strong data residency/KMS requirements. They asked about hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, latency vs cost, and open-model support (Llama, Mistral, other quantized variants). SE agreed to run a short hosted benchmark and share results; AE to send security pack and pricing.

Topics: model selection; context length; multilingual/OCR & tool calling; hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs; security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO).

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription has small errors)
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then Priya will go through model and perf questions. Marcus, do you want to start with a one-line of what you're evaluating?
[00:14] Marcus (Elysian): Sure, thanks. We're Elysian Analytics, we power a multilingual support assistant and document ingestion for enterprise clients. Biggest pain is long documents — contracts, manuals — often 10k to 30k tokens. We need model selection that handles 32k contexts ideally, and also supports tool calling for our vector DB retrieval and a couple internal APIs.
[00:32] Tara (CTO): Yeah, and security is a big deal — we need audit logs, KMS, and SSO. We may go private for some customers but want hosted first to iterate.
[00:44] Jamie: Great, that's the common pattern we see. Priya, want to take the model side?
[00:48] Priya (Redwood SE): Yep. So at a high level Redwood supports a model catalog — open models and optimized variants — and we can run hosted endpoints or dedicated pools, or a private deployment in your VPC for strict isolation. For 32k context you have options: some open models are natively 32k, others we patch via Redwood concat/streaming and KV cache to give effective long contexts. There are also quantized variants for cost.
[01:12] Diego (Elysian): When you say KV cache are you referring to the key-value cache? sometimes folks say KV cash in notes, lol. We want to ensure prefix caching works with our chunking scheme.
[01:24] Priya: Yeah KV cache, typo in notes common. Redwood's runtime maintains a persistent KV cache per session which helps when users browse within a doc — it avoids re-evaluating the whole prefix and reduces token cost. Works with our batching and also with tool-calling flows.
[01:38] Marcus: How do you handle tool-calling? We need structured calls to our retrieval API and an internal invoice-scraper. Can models call out to these reliably?
[01:46] Priya: We support tool/function calling patterns — you can define a schema for the tool, Redwood will surface it to the model and capture the structured output. For hosted we have function-call integrations and you can also run these in dedicated or private with local network access to your internal endpoints.
[02:02] Tara: Is there any difference in latency/cost between hosted and dedicated? For us latency under 300ms for short replies is nice but for long document summarization 2-4s per chunk is ok.
[02:14] Jamie: Right, hosted is the fastest to onboard and is cost-effective for development and small-scale production. Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools and more predictable tail latency, and private gives you the full isolation but is pricier and slower to deploy. If your main customer onboards slowly, we often recommend starting hosted and then moving critical customers to Dedicated or Private.
[02:34] Marcus: Are there models you recommend for multilingual? Our corpus is English, Spanish, French, and some Korean/Chinese.
[02:41] Priya: For multilingual open models Mistral-XX, Llama-3 variants, and some of the larger open instruction models work well. We also have Redwood-curated variants that are fine-tuned and quantized for inference. For Chinese/Korean nuance tests we usually recommend running a small eval because perf varies.
[02:59] Diego: Do you support streaming for partial responses so the UI shows an answer while retrieval continues?
[03:04] Priya: Yes, streaming responses are supported in hosted and dedicated, and function-calling payloads stream as well. For very long contexts we stream partial outputs while the backend fetches continuation chunks or uses the KV cache.
[03:18] Marcus: Cost is a big concern — how do quantized models hit cost vs quality?
[03:24] Priya: Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) lowers GPU memory and cost, but there's a tradeoff in certain tasks. Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles per workload; sometimes we keep a float16 variant for critical steps like generation after retrieval. We can run a quick A/B on your prompts.
[03:40] Tara: On compliance: SOC2, ISO, SSO, audit logs, data residency — what is available out of the box vs add-on?
[03:49] Jamie: SOC2 is standard for Redwood hosted; we also offer enterprise compliance packages for retention policies, longer log retention, and private deployments for data residency. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with our KMS unless you opt for private.
[04:10] Marcus: If we start hosted, how easy is it to move to Dedicated? Do you preserve model versions and routing configs?
[04:16] Priya: Yes, the API and model config layer are consistent. You can pin model versions and rollout policies, and Redwood will route traffic — we can migrate capacity behind the same route with minimal code changes.
[04:27] Diego: About inference performance: can you share any benchmark examples for 32k context? We need to know latency per throughput numbers.
[04:34] Jamie: We'll send a benchmark sheet, but Priya can run a quick hosted perf run using a 32k synthetic doc and your prompts — that'll give real numbers.
[04:42] Priya: Quick note: some open models have quadratic attention costs as context grows; Redwood's runtime picks kernels and optimizations, e.g., Flash attention and custom kv-sharding for longer contexts. That reduces tail latency in practice, but depends on model architecture.
[04:58] Marcus: You mentioned open vs closed models — how about compatibility with OpenAI or Anthropic APIs? We might mix vendors and want consistent latency accounting.
[05:06] Jamie: You can route by policy — cost vs latency vs region — and Redwood exposes per-route metrics. We also support fallbacks to compatible variants if capacity is low. Competitors like OpenAI/Anthropic are common, but customers pick based on cost/quality for specific tasks.
[05:22] Tara: On-tool calling, is there sandboxing or a way to limit what the model can invoke? Security wise we don't want arbitrary calls.
[05:29] Priya: Yes, we have allowlists for tool endpoints and RBAC. In Dedicated/Private you can restrict network egress. All tool calls go through an audit log and you can configure scopes per role.
[05:40] Diego: A nit — how does Redwood handle tokenization differences across models (e.g., tiktoken vs other tokenizers) and how do you normalize cost reporting?
[05:48] Priya: We normalize to token counts per model and show per-token cost in the console. Tokenization differences are surfaced in the SDK, and we provide tokenization preview so you can reconcile costs.
[05:58] Marcus: Ok, now some real constraints — we need: 1) 32k context (must be native or performant via KV), 2) function-calling with schema enforcement, 3) multilingual accuracy, 4) SSO + KMS + audit logs, 5) target P95 latency under 1.5s for typical retrieval-augmented small answers. Is that doable?
[06:20] Jamie: Yes, that's a typical enterprise ask. We'll propose a two-phase POC: Phase 1 hosted perf + eval to validate model quality and latency; Phase 2 dedicated pool for one or two production customers for isolation and predictable latency.
[06:31] Tara: What about pricing — ballpark for hosted vs dedicated?
[06:35] Jamie: I'll share a pricing sheet. Ballpark: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated is a committed monthly GPU pool; private includes platform fee. Exact numbers depend on model mix and qps. We'll include an example using your prompt sets.
[06:47] Diego: Any gotchas for running inference on Korean/Chinese? We've seen hallucinations increase with some open models.
[06:53] Priya: That's why we recommend run-of-eval with your corpora. Also, some models have been finetuned on multilingual data and perform better; quantization can affect tokenization and sometimes degrade non-Latin languages — we'll surface that in the eval.
[07:08] Marcus: For the hosted perf run, what inputs do you need?
[07:11] Priya: Ideally 3 prompt sets: 1) doc-to-summary (long doc 20-32k tokens), 2) question-answering via RAG, 3) multilingual customer messages. Also sample tool schemas, and target SLA. Diego will provide those.
[07:24] Diego: I'll dump the datasets to the secure S3 link and share with you by Friday. Note: some docs are PII — we need assurances on retention.
[07:33] Jamie: We'll mark the test bucket only for perf and redact stored logs on request; we'll include retention controls in the security pack.
[07:42] Tara: One more — how long does a private deployment take? If we need full VPC/on-prem for a client in Q1, timeline?
[07:49] Jamie: Private deployments are typically 6-10 weeks depending on infra approvals and networking. Dedicated is faster for enterprise (1-3 weeks) once contracts are signed.
[07:58] Marcus: Great. Any other questions from team?
[08:02] Tara: No, good. Thanks.
[08:05] Jamie: Ok recap: we will share security docs and pricing (Jamie), Priya will run hosted perf with Elysian prompt sets and share results, Diego to share prompt sets and data, we'll schedule a follow-up SE deep dive week of Nov 22.
[08:19] Marcus: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:22] Jamie: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the pack.
